request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 0 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run to assess consistency. A config that wins consistently across folds is more trustworthy than one with high variance. (Independent run 1.)

concerns: The LightGBM (run 1) advantage over logistic (run 4) is 0.0424 PR-AUC. That is below one fold SD (about 0.061-0.064), so by the stated rule the simpler logistic model wins.

Paired by fold, run 1 beats run 4 in 4 of 5 folds (+0.10, +0.056, +0.031, +0.030, -0.007). This is a modest consistent edge, so reasonable reviewers could prefer LightGBM, and that is why confidence is only moderate.
Fold-to-fold PR-AUC varies a lot (about 0.61-0.80) with only 5 folds and about 500 positives. The ranking among the top configs is statistically fragile.

ROC-AUC is about 0.94 for every model family, and the models are all very close on it. This suggests a strong, easily learned signal, possibly from size or volume proxies or from a label generated by rules on the same features. It may not reflect true fraud, since the label origin is undocumented.
Precision@50 of 0.74-0.78 is high. It is plausible for a flagged-suspicion label but should not be read as confirmed fraud-detection accuracy.

Only 4 configs were tried, with no tuning of LightGBM or logistic beyond a single setting each. Nothing is known about whether the CV was grouped or time-aware. The claims window is under a year, so leakage across folds is possible.

Run 4 uses the agent features with class_weight, while the best LightGBM uses no imbalance handling and no agent features. The comparison is confounded across feature sets, so I cannot isolate the effect of model type.
The audit queue of about 100 providers is deeper than the precision@50 metric reported, so queue-level precision at 100 is unverified.
